title: The Cipher of the Green Zone Anew
premise: Cyrus Crane, a disgraced intelligence analyst living off unattributable freelance work, is hired to trace a voiceprint that unlocks a black server in Nairobi. He discovers the server belongs to Meridian, the deniable training network that manufactured analysts like him—and that it holds extraction lists, kill orders, and his own file. As Meridian's cleaners close in and a former classmate turned handler plays both sides, Cyrus must decide whether justice means exposure or destruction. He burns the network's core from inside its own safehouse, sends the evidence to the one journalist who will print it, and boards the dawn flight knowing he has traded his invisibility for a name he can finally own.
about_author: S. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent years adjacent to the intelligence community before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about institutional rot and the people who survive it.

chapters.title: The Work Nobody Signs
chapters.summary: Cyrus Crane, POV. Broke and blacklisted after three agency exits, Cyrus takes a cash job verifying a voiceprint for a lawyer who won't give his name. The beat is weary competence—Cyrus is good at being nobody, and it's costing him everything but survival.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The voiceprint matches a dead man—or a man erased—and unlocks a server in Nairobi holding files stamped with a logo Cyrus recognizes from his own training days. The emotional beat is dread: the past he buried has an IP address.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV, with an intercut of a cleaner named Voss receiving orders. Cyrus confirms the server belongs to Meridian, the off-books network that trained him, and finds his own redacted file among the extraction lists. Beat: vertigo—he was never a freelancer; he was inventory.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Cyrus and Nadia Reyes, his former classmate now working Meridian's edges. Nadia contacts him claiming she wants out too, offering access in exchange for trust. The beat is seductive hope shadowed by Cyrus's trained suspicion of every gift.

chapters.title: Nairobi Protocol
chapters.summary: Cyrus flies to Nairobi under a borrowed identity while Voss tracks the same trail behind him. In a cybercafé he pulls partial archives: kill orders dressed as personnel actions. Beat: cold fury hardening into purpose—this stops being survival and becomes a case.

chapters.title: What the Training Was For
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV, with flashbacks to his recruitment. Trapped between Voss's sweep and a Meridian trap, he realizes the network designed analysts to burn out and vanish—expendable by design. Beat: grief for the version of himself who believed the work meant something.

chapters.title: The Turn
chapters.summary: Nadia, POV. Nadia betrays Cyrus's location to Meridian to buy her own extraction, then wavers when she sees her name on the next purge list. Beat: the corrupting bargain—she chose power over loyalty and discovers the price was always going to be her.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Captured and brought to Meridian's regional safehouse, Cyrus faces the director who built him, offered reinstatement if he hands over the archive copy. Beat: temptation as interrogation—the system offering to forgive him for becoming what it made.

chapters.title: Burn
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Cyrus and Voss. Using protocols only a Meridian-trained analyst knows, Cyrus turns the safehouse's own systems against it, wipes the operational core, and routes the evidence to journalist Lena Okafor as Voss breaches the room. Nadia dies covering his exit. Beat: righteous destruction at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Dawn Flight
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Wounded, stripped of every alias, he reaches the airstrip as Okafor's first story breaks and Meridian's survivors scatter. He boards with nothing but his real name and the knowledge that justice outside the law still leaves a bill. Beat: exhausted, earned peace—not clean, but his.
